channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Members Only 2026 · K Space Contemporary
item.description: Juried, non-thematic exhibition of new work by members of K Space Contemporary, the 501(c)(3) contemporary art space in downtown Corpus Christi. Held only in even-numbered years, it exists to put a member's work in front of a panel of Coastal Bend art professionals: the Best of Show winner is awarded a solo exhibition at K Space in 2027 or 2028, with cash awards for second and third place. All visual art media are accepted, including photography - the gallery bars only reproductions such as giclee or inkjet copies of original works, and video is exhibited on a 58-inch screen. Each artist may submit one or two works completed in the last two years and not previously shown at K Space; 40 to 50 top-scoring works are hung. Two-dimensional work must be no wider than 60 inches and wired to hang, with Plexi rather than glass. Entry is $10 plus K Space membership, which can be bought inside the entry system ($20 student or senior 65+, $35 individual). All work must be for sale, with a 40% gallery commission. Notification November 12; the show runs November 28, 2026 to January 22, 2027, with an ArtWalk reception and awards on December 4. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $10 + membership ($20-$35). Prize: Solo exhibition + cash awards.

item.title: 2026 New Exhibiting Members · Buffalo Society of Artists
item.description: Annual jury for exhibiting membership of the Buffalo Society of Artists, founded in 1891 and one of the oldest artist societies in the United States. Exhibiting membership is the gate to the Society's juried programme - the annual Catalogue Exhibition, the Open Members show, the Summer and Thumb Box exhibitions - and its 226 current exhibiting members include working photographers, so a photographic practice is judged on the same footing as painting or printmaking. Applicants upload a resume, a brief artist statement and 9 to 13 works made in the last three years; video artists submit a single MP4 of up to ten minutes instead. Three of the uploaded works must then be brought as originals to an in-person review on Saturday, October 10 at Our Lady of Hope Parish in Buffalo, drop-off 9:30-10:15am and pick-up by 1pm. The seven-member review panel is named in advance and includes two photographers - Christina Buscarino, gallerist of the C. Stuart and Jane H. Hunt Art Gallery, and Nate Ely, education director at CEPA - alongside Hallwalls deputy director Parrish Gibbons; it scores each applicant on artist statement, innovation, technical facility, presentation and exhibition history. Open to artists 18 or over who currently live in Western New York and are not enrolled in an undergraduate visual arts degree. The $25 jurying fee is non-refundable, the application window runs September 1 to midnight on October 2, 2026, decisions are sent by mail by October 17, and accepted artists then pay $50 annual dues. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Exhibition membership.

item.title: Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships 2027
item.description: Annual fellowship programme from Vital Impacts, the 501(c)(3) co-founded by photographer Ami Vitale, supporting visual storytellers working on long-term documentary projects about environmental and conservation issues. For 2027 the foundation awards one $20,000 fellowship to an established environmental photographer, named for Dr. Jane Goodall, six $5,000 fellowships to emerging photographers, and ten places on an intensive mentorship programme; one fellow is also invited to exhibit at the 2027 Festival of Ethical Photography in Lodi, Italy. Recipients have twelve months to develop their project with publishing and showcase support from Vital Impacts. The foundation strongly favours photographers with a meaningful, sustained relationship to the community, place or issue they propose to document, and is drawn to work that moves past documenting environmental problems to the people and initiatives working toward solutions. You do not have to live permanently in a place to qualify - recurring travel, long-term collaboration or professional and academic engagement also count. Prior publication experience is not required, and applicants may write in their native language, with translation arranged. Submit 20 images from one or two bodies of work plus a synopsis, project statement and biography. Applications open August 31, 2026 on Picter; the $25 fee is waived for applicants from developing countries and on request for economic hardship. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $25 (waivers available). Prize: $20,000 + 6 × $5,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: We: Culture · CICA Museum
item.description: International group exhibition at CICA Museum in Gimpo, South Korea, gathering work on culture in its many registers - multiculturalism, identity, subcultures, social media culture, pop culture, and ideas of nation, religion and race. Photography is named first among the welcomed media and "Photographs & 2D Digital Art" is one of four submission categories alongside video and interactive art, physical works, and performance. Submission is free and by email: up to five JPEGs and/or three links to video works, plus a bio. Selected photographic and digital work is printed at 10x15 or 10x10 inches, framed and installed by the museum's team; artists sending physical work ship at their own cost, with 2D pieces capped at 39 inches on the longest side and wall-mounted work at 10 kg. Accepted artists contribute $78 USD (110,000 KRW) per piece toward exhibition processing and maintenance. The show runs April 28 - May 16, 2027, and the museum notes the dates are subject to change. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $78 per accepted work. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: After Love: Broken Hearts & Broken Bodies · OVADA
item.description: Group exhibition at OVADA's warehouse gallery in central Oxford inviting artists to respond to romantic heartbreak, relationship breakdown and the strategies we use to survive love's endings. The show is part of a four-century historical study of heartbreak as an embodied emotion by Dr Sally Holloway, funded by an Arts & Humanities Research Council fellowship, with partners including Oxfordshire Mind and the Poetry Pharmacy. OVADA calls it a radically inclusive exhibition where all eligible works will be shown - there is no jury - and the hang is arranged salon style by Audrey Baldwin and Sally Holloway as work arrives on install day. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, collage, textiles, printmaking, ceramics, sculpture and video; work must be wall-hung or free-standing and no larger than 2m x 2m. Up to three works per artist. Open to artists 18 and over resident in the UK; work must be delivered in person on Saturday 3 October and collected on 18 or 19 October, as the gallery cannot accept posted submissions. Images of exhibited work also appear in an ArtSteps digital version of the show. The exhibition runs 7-18 October 2026, with a launch on the evening of 7 October. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: £10 (1 work), £15 (2 works), £20 (3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: In the Moment · PhotoMidwest
item.description: Members' exhibition mounted as part of PhotoMidwest's 2026 Biennial Festival, shown at the University of Wisconsin's Pyle Center in Madison and in the organisation's online gallery. Each PhotoMidwest member may enter one image, free of charge, on any subject - the show is framed around photography's ability to make a moment permanent, whether it documents a slice of reality or a vision from the artist's imagination. There is no jury: the Pyle Center has wall space for about 75 framed pieces and, if more entries arrive than there is wall, they are hung in the order they were entered, first come first served. Every entry appears in the online gallery regardless, and members who would rather not frame can enter for the online gallery only. Framed work is capped at 30 inches on the longest dimension; files should be 2000-2500 pixels on the long edge, sRGB, under 2.5 MB, with no watermarks or borders. The exhibition runs November 2, 2026 - January 29, 2027. Entry requires PhotoMidwest membership. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: IMPRINT · The Hook Experiment
item.description: A juried international group exhibition about the impressions that shape us — the visible and invisible traces of memory, identity, history and human experience, and the stories we inherit, rewrite or leave behind. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, assemblage, wood, glass, ceramics and collage; video, electronics and anything needing power are excluded, and every finished work must measure exactly 10 x 10 inches. The Hook Experiment is a 4,500-square-foot gallery and creative space in a partially renovated building on Oxford, Pennsylvania's main street, founded to give artists room for risk and imperfection outside commercial pressure. Selected work hangs November 20, 2026 – January 16, 2027 with opening and closing receptions plus school and community engagement events; artists keep 70% of sales and may mark work NFS. Artists ship both ways with a prepaid return label or hand-deliver on November 7–8. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $25 (up to 3 works) / $5 each additional, max 6. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: YICCA Prize 26/27
item.description: An international contemporary art prize run since 2010 by the Italian association A.P.S. MOHO, open to artists and groups of any nationality with no qualification requirements; all techniques are accepted, photography included, and works may be up to 3 x 3 metres. A jury selects 18 artists for the final exhibition at the New Art Space, Cannaregio 883, Venice, running November 14–28, 2026, and selected work is published in the YICCA catalogue, distributed free to finalists and to the collectors, press and curators invited to the opening. Cash prizes total €5,500 — €3,000 first, €1,000 second, €500 third and a €1,000 prize reserved for students — paid by the main sponsor by bank transfer, and scored one third each by the jury, the association and the host gallery. The jury roster is due to be published before the entry deadline. Artists carry shipping and any insurance on exhibited work. — Deadline: October 8, 2026. Fee: €50 (1 work) – €160 (6 works). Prize: €5,500 in cash prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: Visual Languages Across Cultures — ZAO Magazine · Molend Art
item.description: A guest-edited special issue of ZAO, the independent art magazine published in Glasgow by Molend Art and carrying an ISSN assigned through the British Library. The issue asks how contemporary art becomes a shared language across cultures, and looks for work reflecting on cultural diaspora, identity, memory and cross-cultural communication. All mediums are accepted — painting, sculpture, photography, installation, ceramics, mixed media, digital media, performance documentation, textile and experimental practices — from artists 18 and over worldwide at any career stage, up to six original works each. Guest editor Mengyi Grace Wang, a contemporary artist and researcher, works with editor-in-chief Bowen Wu. ZAO favours practices that are still unfolding and builds a cultural passage between East Asia and the UK. Free to enter; AI-generated work is strictly prohibited. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — December 2026 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview, and there is no word limit on the artist's own account of the work. The jurors read the documents as well as the images. The submission window for the December issue runs October 1–20, 2026; email submissions. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Portrait 2026 — Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: A juried exhibition celebrating portraiture and the stories carried in the human face and body, open to photographers worldwide. Juror Alan K. Avery, president and owner of Alan Avery Art Company, Atlanta's longest-running gallery, selects up to 24 works. Themes include identity and self-expression, emotion and psychology, cultural diversity and narrative portraiture. Selected prints (24 inches maximum on the longest side, white or black frames and mats) hang at the APG Gallery in Atlanta from November 3 to December 4, 2026. — Deadline: September 23, 2026. Fee: $30–$95 (members) / $30–$70 (students). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Storytelling 2026: Documentary and Street Photography · Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: A juried exhibition of street and documentary photography with a strong narrative pull — candid everyday life, city shadows, an abandoned country road, quiet moments of joy, humour, love or anxiety, in the lineage of Arbus, Frank, Koudelka, Levitt, DeCarava, Mary Ellen Mark and Gordon Parks. Juror Karen Marshall chairs the Documentary Practice and Visual Journalism Program at the International Center of Photography. Selected prints (32 inches maximum on the longest side, white or black frames and mats) hang at the APG Gallery in Atlanta from November 3 to December 4, 2026. — Deadline: September 23, 2026. Fee: $30–$95 (members) / $30–$70 (students). Prize: None listed.

item.title: 2027 Soulangh AiR Program
item.description: Soulangh Cultural Park occupies the buildings of the Jiali Sugar Factory, which opened in 1906 as the Meiji Sugar Corporation's first modern refinery and ran until 1995; award-winning Taiwanese architects converted its Japanese-era warehouses into a cultural park that opened to the public in 2005. Its artist-in-residence programme has run since 2013 and is open to all artistic disciplines, worldwide. The 2027 theme asks artists to reinterpret the stories of Tainan through sugar, salt or local cultural heritage - Jiali District sits at the geographical centre of Tainan's Saline Land, was an essential place of habitation for the Siraya people, and is still rich in Taoist temples and centipede parades. Residents need to be able to do field research and to plan and manage their own project, and are encouraged to work with the park's environment, including outdoor pieces. Each artist gets an accommodation suite with utilities included, a bicycle, an exhibition space fitted with lighting rails, wooden partitions and air conditioning, a shared studio, and free use of the park's projectors, monitors, speakers, lights and hardware tools. The funding comes in three parts: living expenses of up to NT$800 per day for up to 90 days (NT$72,000), an exhibition production fee of up to NT$200 per day for up to 90 days (NT$18,000), and a production budget of NT$150,000 covering exhibit materials, woodwork, painting and printing, 500 flyers, translation, artwork insurance, an opening press conference and workshop materials. Amounts are set by the review committee and are subject to 6-20 per cent withholding tax for foreign artists, who also pay a stamp duty of 0.1 per cent of the grant in cash. In return each resident stages one achievement exhibition and at least one parent-child workshop or open studio day before the residency ends, and files a report. Applicants need basic English or Chinese, a residency project plan, a CV and at least one recommendation letter carrying a handwritten signature. Copyright in the work stays with the artist, though the park may exhibit and publish it for educational and promotional purposes. The residency period runs 1 March to 30 October 2027 and applicants select three preferred terms; artists who do not stay for at least two-thirds of their term are disqualified. Applications go through the Tainan City Government's AIR in Tainan portal and results are announced in November 2026. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + NT$72,000 grant + NT$150,000 production budget.

item.title: FULL CIRCLE · PARC Art Gallery
item.description: PARC Art Gallery is the nonprofit gallery inside the Plymouth Arts & Recreation Complex in Michigan, a building shared by more than thirty independent arts, education and recreation organisations. It is directed and curated by Élevé Art Gallery and is open to the public seven days a week, 10am to 8pm. FULL CIRCLE asks for original 2D and 3D work about cycles, connection and return: the seasons, growth, repetition and the passage of time; relationships, community and the ways people and places are linked; coming back to a person, place, memory or tradition; circles, rings, spirals and spheres as visual form; and ideas of completion, balance and wholeness. The gallery calls these starting points rather than requirements, and says it is drawn to work that invites viewers to look twice - to notice a pattern, connection or relationship that is not immediately apparent. Photography is named in the gallery's own list of eligible original media, alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, mixed media and original digital illustration, and photographs are specifically exempted from the ban on prints; giclee and fine-art reproductions of an existing painting, drawing or photograph are not eligible, and no AI-generated work of any kind is accepted. Entry is $35, non-refundable, for one to three pieces. Work must be original, independently completed without instruction, previously unshown at PARC, offered for sale, dry and finished, and suitable for all ages - the gallery serves visitors from toddlers upward and reserves the discretion to decline submissions on that basis. 2D work must hang on a wire (no plastic-covered wires, clips or sawtooth hangers), be professionally framed or have finished edges, and stay within 60 inches wide and 40lbs; 3D work must be freestanding, no taller than 40 inches and no heavier than 100lbs. Open to artists 18 and over who live or work in Michigan, with artists from elsewhere considered case by case provided the work can be dropped off and collected in person; if shipping is the only option the artist pays all costs. Notifications go out 6 September, drop-off is 8 September from 10am to noon, and the exhibition runs 10 September to 1 November 2026. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Adler Gallery Exhibition — January–February 2027 · Port Washington Public Library
item.description: The Karen and Ed Adler Gallery at Port Washington Public Library gives one artist at a time a two-month solo exhibition in a dedicated gallery space, and there is an opening in the schedule for January-February 2027. Submissions are read by the library's Art Advisory Council: a preview committee makes the first cut and the full council then votes on whether to extend an invitation, with preview meetings held three times a year. During the run the artist is offered a two-hour public reception to talk about the work. Entry is free. Applicants fill in the library's own request form with a current resume and ten high-quality images of individual works, each labelled by title in the filename, tightly cropped so only the artwork shows, with no borders or backgrounds, and photographed straight on rather than at an angle; an image list giving title, medium and dimensions for each work is asked for, and a bio or promotional material can be attached as optional additional information. The library asks for a cohesive selection that reads as a curated exhibit rather than a survey. Only artists currently living in the tri-state area - New York, New Jersey and Connecticut - will be considered. Photography is part of the gallery's programme: past Adler Gallery shows include Steve Lampasona's The Light and Textures of New York City, a Holocaust survivor photography exhibit mounted around International Holocaust Remembrance Day, and Alan Richards's Let Me Show You Something, which built on archival and vintage photographs enhanced with drawing and digital painting. The exhibition runs 29 December 2026 to 28 February 2027. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Two-month solo exhibition.

item.title: Homage | The Americans · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Part of the Griffin Museum's State of Our Union series, this online exhibition pays homage to Robert Frank, who crossed the country in 1958 with a camera and a Guggenheim and came back with a book that changed the way America saw itself. The museum describes The Americans as controversial and unflattering, a stark look at post-war America and a mirror the country did not know it needed - diners and gas stations, funerals and flags, jukeboxes and segregated buses. This call places Frank's original vision in dialogue with photographers working today who have inherited his instinct: the drive to look past the myth of the country and toward the lived reality of it. The museum invites photographers everywhere to contribute new work in direct homage to The Americans - images carrying forward Frank's willingness to look honestly, his eye for the overlooked corner and the unguarded face, and his belief that a nation is best understood not through its monuments but through its people. Entrants are asked to send their homage to Frank, their vision of America, and to say how Frank inspired them as a photographer. The online exhibition runs October 1 to 30, 2026. It sits in the Griffin Museum's 2026 Online Exhibition Program, which puts out a new open call each quarter on themes drawn from the museum's own exhibition schedule. Entry is free, global and open to anyone - the museum states plainly that 'our online exhibitions are always free of entry, global and open'. Submissions go through a Google Form; files must be sRGB JPGs sized between 1200 and 2000 pixels on the longest side and under 1.2 MB, or they are disqualified. Work is reviewed by the museum's in-house curatorial team with final selection by Executive Director Crista Dix. Recent online calls have drawn between 200 and 400 entries. Online exhibitions run one to one-and-a-half months; selected artists get a social media package ahead of the opening, and some shows generate guest-juror Critic's Picks or artist Q&As. Copyright stays with the artist throughout. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: To the Sea · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: The Griffin Museum wants photographs of water in all its moods - a wave breaking, the horizon at sunset, fog rolling over the harbour, a quiet cove, a storm coming in. The museum frames the theme around a pull that is older than any of us: summers at the beach, winter walks in the sand, storm waves against the shore, and the stories about what lies beneath the tideline that have filled imaginations for generations with monsters, demons and sirens just past what we can see. To the Sea is an invitation to capture that connection, whether from the shoreline, a pier, or simply watching the tide come in - every photograph a small piece of a much older story about why, no matter how far we wander, we always find our way back to the water's edge. The online exhibition runs 5 October 2026 to 1 January 2027, the longest of the museum's current online shows. It sits in the Griffin Museum's 2026 Online Exhibition Program, which puts out a new open call each quarter on themes drawn from the museum's own exhibition schedule. Entry is free, global and open to anyone - the museum states plainly that 'our online exhibitions are always free of entry, global and open'. Submissions go through a Google Form; files must be sRGB JPGs sized between 1200 and 2000 pixels on the longest side and under 1.2 MB, or they are disqualified. Work is reviewed by the museum's in-house curatorial team with final selection by Executive Director Crista Dix. Recent online calls have drawn between 200 and 400 entries. Online exhibitions run one to one-and-a-half months; selected artists get a social media package ahead of the opening, and some shows generate guest-juror Critic's Picks or artist Q&As. Copyright stays with the artist throughout. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Earth, Wind & Fire · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Long before they were a force in music, earth, wind and fire were forces of nature - and the Griffin Museum wants photographs that find them at work in the American landscape. Wind moving through tall grass or across a mountain ridge; fire as the warmth of a sunset, the glow of golden hour, the last light before dusk; earth in the shape of every hill, canyon and shoreline built up over centuries. The museum points to the deserts of the Southwest, the wheat fields of the Midwest, the granite coast of New England and the wide open sky of the plains, and asks for work that celebrates the elemental beauty of a country these forces are still shaping - fog lifting off a New England mountain at dawn, sunlight breaking through storm clouds over open farmland, the textures of stone, sand and soil under changing American light. The call is part of the museum's State of Our Union series and the online exhibition runs November 1 to 30, 2026. It sits in the Griffin Museum's 2026 Online Exhibition Program, which puts out a new open call each quarter on themes drawn from the museum's own exhibition schedule. Entry is free, global and open to anyone - the museum states plainly that 'our online exhibitions are always free of entry, global and open'. Submissions go through a Google Form; files must be sRGB JPGs sized between 1200 and 2000 pixels on the longest side and under 1.2 MB, or they are disqualified. Work is reviewed by the museum's in-house curatorial team with final selection by Executive Director Crista Dix. Recent online calls have drawn between 200 and 400 entries. Online exhibitions run one to one-and-a-half months; selected artists get a social media package ahead of the opening, and some shows generate guest-juror Critic's Picks or artist Q&As. Copyright stays with the artist throughout. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: SOUTHWEST Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Decode Gallery's juried exhibition on the landscapes, cultures and stories of the American Southwest. Images must have been captured in California, Nevada, Utah, Colorado, Arizona or New Mexico - the vibrant colours of the desert, the rich history of the region, or the spirit of its people - but the call itself is open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional alike. Twenty-six images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Epson Ultra Premium Luster paper and presents work in museum-quality 22 x 22 inch white frames with precut white mats in a range of sizes, scaling files for the best fit without ever cropping them. One print is made per accepted image and archived in a flat file for six months after the show. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due two days later. The exhibition runs December 5 to 26, 2026 in Tucson, opening December 5. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with the gallery taking a 50 per cent commission and all rights to the file and the print remaining with the photographer. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: All About Women 2026 · Marin Society of Artists
item.description: The Marin Society of Artists has run a gallery and artist community in San Rafael, California since 1927, and All About Women is its annual online exhibition about women's lives - past, present and future - and the issues that concern them. It is open to all artists aged 18 and over regardless of gender, and photography is named in the accepted-media list alongside painting, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media, fiber art, ceramics and all types of fine art craft; film and video are the only exclusions. The juror is Nancy Roberts, a professional artist and educator based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Selected work is presented in two forms: an online show in the MSA Virtual Gallery, which carries each artist's price and contact information, and a video version of the whole exhibition that stays available on YouTube after the show closes. A virtual Zoom reception is held on 11 October 2026 at 5pm PST. Awards are $500 first prize, $300 second and $100 third, plus several non-monetary honourable mentions, and MSA takes no commission on work sold. Entry is through CaFE: $35 for three pieces for non-members and $30 for MSA members, then $7 for each additional piece up to a total of ten; diptychs and triptychs count as one piece and should be submitted as a single image. Work previously juried into an MSA exhibition is not accepted. Entries close 15 September 2026 at 11:59pm Mountain Time and the exhibition runs 29 September to 30 November 2026. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $35 non-members (3 entries, +$7 each up to 10). Prize: $500 / $300 / $100.

item.title: ICOSA Annual 2026 · ICOSA Collective
item.description: ICOSA is an artist-run non-profit cooperative gallery in the Canopy Arts Complex on the east side of Austin, Texas, and has staged more than 80 exhibitions since 2015 alongside sound installations, film screenings and performances. ICOSA Annual is its national juried group show and the main route for non-member artists to exhibit in the gallery, timed to run in tandem with the Austin Studio Tour - a free, self-guided art event spanning two weekends that brought over 4,000 visitors to ICOSA in 2025. The juror is Dennis Nance, curator at the Galveston Arts Center since 2016 and previously Exhibitions and Programming Director at Lawndale Art Center in Houston, a practising artist who has shown at the Contemporary Arts Museum Houston and the ICA Boston's Art Lab. The call is open to all US residents working in any 2D or 3D media and video. Applicants send an artist statement and CV of no more than three pages, five to ten images of work completed in the past two years and, optionally, up to five minutes of video via an unlocked YouTube or Vimeo link; no prices or price sheets. Entry is $30, and thanks to an anonymous donor ICOSA can waive it for ten artists experiencing financial hardship - email icosaannual@gmail.com before starting the application. Notifications go out 16 October 2026, shipped work must arrive by 6 November and hand-delivered work on 7 November, and the exhibition runs 13 to 22 November 2026 with an opening reception on the 13th from 7 to 10pm and a meet-and-greet with the curator at the close. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: The Space Between Storms · Emotions Matter
item.description: Emotions Matter is a New York 501(c)(3) that runs peer support groups, education and advocacy for people affected by borderline personality disorder, and its BPD Art Show has been going since 2017. The fifth edition, 'The Space Between Storms: Borderline Personality Disorder Beyond the Moments You See', asks for work about the moments that usually go unseen - the space between crises, and the experience of hope, healing, recovery, identity and ordinary life with BPD. It is open to anyone with lived experience of BPD as an individual, a family member or a professional, anywhere in the world. Submissions are one to three original 2D or 3D artworks with a separate artist statement for each piece addressing the work, its connection to the theme and the applicant's own BPD journey; statements go to the jurors only and are not published without permission. Nothing is shipped - the show is virtual and judged from uploaded images, with selected artists supplying a high-resolution file afterwards. This year the show sits inside a three-night virtual BPD Art Festival in the week of 26 October 2026, with selected work in a virtual exhibit on the Emotions Matter site and an optional live Artists Roundtable. Selected artists sign a waiver allowing display but retain ownership of their work throughout. The $40 entry fee offsets technology, printing and administrative costs; a limited number of entry-fee scholarships are available first come, first served to applicants in financial hardship, by email to info@emotionsmatterbpd.org. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Grants to Individuals - 2027 Cycle · Graham Foundation
item.description: The Graham Foundation for Advanced Studies in the Fine Arts has funded independent work on architecture and the designed environment from its Chicago base since 1956, and its Grants to Individuals programme is one of the few places a self-directed photographer can get a book, an exhibition or a long research trip paid for outright. Two grant types are on offer. Production and Presentation grants cover the cost of realising and publicly presenting a project - exhibitions, installations, films, videos, new media and web-based initiatives, publications and other public programmes - and do not exceed $20,000, with awards generally running $5,000 to $15,000; these require a committed producer or presenting partner already in place when the inquiry form goes in. Research and Development grants cover travel, archival research, documentation, materials and supplies, do not exceed $10,000 and generally run $5,000 to $10,000, and need no producer. The Foundation names no medium, and its own grantee roster settles the question: Kate Joyce holds a 2026 publication grant for Watt or Fall, made across a year-long residency photographing Fallingwater, a building the Foundation's own citation calls one that defies its visual representation; Noritaka Minami has been funded three times, most recently in 2025 for a photographic study of the concrete pillboxes of Hokkaido; and Zoe Leonard (Al Rio/To the River), Camilo Jose Vergara (Tracking Newark, N.J., 1977-2024), Ashley Hunt (a photographic survey of more than 250 US prisons), David Schalliol, George Legrady, Leonardo Finotti and Jason Oddy have all been funded as individuals for bodies of photographic work on the built environment. What the Foundation wants is a project that creates and communicates significant ideas about architecture and the designed environment, takes a position, brings work into the public realm and amplifies emerging and underrecognised perspectives - first-time applicants get particular attention. Grantmaking focuses on the United States but the Foundation also awards internationally; funded projects must include meaningful public dissemination in English. Work done in pursuit of an academic degree is not funded (advanced doctoral candidates go to the separate Carter Manny Award instead), only one grant application may be made per year, and no more than 30 per cent of the request may go to the applicant's own fee. Applying is free and two-stage: an inquiry form by 15 September 2026 at 5 pm Central, invitations to submit a full proposal in December 2026 to January 2027, proposals due February 2027, decisions 31 May 2027 and the earliest project start date 15 June 2027. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000-$20,000.

item.title: CAL Fall 2026 Judged Show · Conroe Art League
item.description: The Conroe Art League's autumn judged show is run virtually on CaFE, with winning work by adult CAL members invited into the league's Madeley Fine Art Gallery in downtown Conroe for the month of October — no hanging fee, but one docent shift per artwork. Photography is a category of its own: the league asks that photographic images be the artist's own, made on film or digitally on a lens-based camera and produced by photographic processes, minimally altered with standard post-processing. The AI line is drawn unusually tightly — no stock or AI images in any form, nothing substantial imported from another image, and no AI sharpening or resolution tools such as Adobe super resolution or Topaz Photo AI. Judging is by Diann Zimmerman, an artist and educator who founded the Watercolor — Beginners and Beyond community and was Education Director for the Watercolor Art Society-Houston. Cash awards, scaled to the number of paid entries, go to Best of Show, Best Floral, Best Landscape and Best Student; the amounts are not published in advance, and the Best of Show winner also receives a year's CAL membership. Winners qualify to enter the Lone Star Art Guild's 2027 annual show, though that step requires membership of CAL or another LSAG league. Entry is open to any artist living in Texas, member or not; entries from outside Texas are declined. Work must be original, not painted on by anyone else, and completed in the last two years. Two-dimensional work is capped at 48 inches including the frame and 30 pounds; three-dimensional work at 30 x 30 x 48 inches and 40 pounds. Subject matter must be family friendly and no nudes are accepted. Adults pay $20 per artwork — the league states no maximum, though the CaFE form takes up to 20 images per artist — while artists 18 and under enter up to three works free using the coupon codes published with the call. Awards are announced electronically on Friday 2 October, with gallery take-in for eligible winners on 6 October. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $20 per artwork (free for students 18 and under). Prize: Cash awards.

item.title: Eighth Annual Online Juried Exhibition · The Idaherma Museum of Art Foundation
item.description: The Idaherma Museum of Art Foundation, a small Princeton-based 501(c)(3) set up to find and promote artists worldwide, runs an annual online juried show with real money behind it: the David Latin Williams Foundation award of $250, second prize $150, third $100 and two honourable mentions of $50 each, all posted out to the winners. Every accepted entrant gets at least one work shown, not only the prizewinners — the foundation publishes each edition as a browsable online exhibition captioned by medium. This year's juror is Elizabeth Massa, a New Jersey photographer, printmaker and teaching artist who holds a graduate certificate in documentary photography from the Salt Institute and studied street photography in Venice; her statement asks for work with a distinct point of view — how you interact with the materials of your medium, how you see the world around you, how your work reflects the objects of daily life, travel, the natural world or your dreams — and says plainly that the show is open to all visual media. The foundation's eligibility line still asks for original works on paper, but its own exhibitions have never been held to that: ten of the 120 works in the fourth annual show are photographs, oil and acrylic on canvas are throughout, and a photograph took second prize in the seventh. Work must be original and not made in any class or with any instructor within the last three years. Nothing is mailed: work is judged and displayed from files, sized between 5 x 8 and 24 x 36 inches, with the long edge no more than 1500 pixels, at least 72 dpi, unwatermarked, unframed, in JPG or PNG. Open to artists 18 and over. AI-generated work is not accepted, and the foundation reserves the right to display submitted work for one year. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $25 first entry, $5 each additional. Prize: $250 + $150 + $100.

item.title: 2026 Small Works Show · Art League of New Britain
item.description: The Art League of New Britain's annual holiday-season show of work made on an intimate scale, on view 28 November to 20 December 2026 with an opening reception on Saturday 28 November from 3 to 5 pm. This one is non-juried: every submitted artwork is accepted, there is no juror and the league lists its awards as none, so what is on offer is a month of wall space in a real gallery rather than a prize. Each artist is given a designated area that the ALNB gallery team hangs. All original media are accepted and the league runs its own annual photography juried exhibition, but digital art, including AI-generated imagery, is not eligible. The total combined unframed width of one artist's works may not exceed 14 inches; 2D work must arrive ready to hang on wire or D-rings, with no sawtooth hangers or easel-back frames, and wall reliefs are capped at 8 inches deep and 40 pounds. Every piece must be listed for sale at $35 or more and stay on display until the show closes, sold or not, though a sold work may be replaced for another entry fee. Open to artists 18 and over with original work made in the past three years that has not been shown at ALNB before. Up to five entries at $15 each, $10 for members, registered through the league's own online portal by 20 November at 11:59 pm; the league's record for the show also flags a gallery-sitting requirement. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $15 per entry (members $10). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artistic Production Grant — Spring 2027 Cycle · VIA Art Fund
item.description: VIA Art Fund's Artistic Production Grants pay for the production of newly commissioned works of visual art shown outside museum or gallery walls, in the public realm or in non-traditional exhibition environments. Awards run from $25,000 to $100,000, with the upper levels reserved for permanent installations or works to be gifted to a US public collection, and the fund has awarded more than $10 million since 2013. The Spring 2027 cycle starts with a letter of inquiry due 5 November 2026; invitations to submit a full application go out 15 December 2026, invited applications are due 25 January 2027, awards are announced in April 2027 and projects must open to the public after 15 June 2027. Individual artists, nonprofits and cultural institutions may apply, in the US and internationally, but the project needs both a confirmed artist and a confirmed exhibition venue or presenting partner at the time of the letter of inquiry: if the project takes place in the US the artist may be based anywhere, and if the venue is outside the US the artist must be based in the US. VIA does not fund museum or gallery exhibitions, curatorial projects, residency programmes, performing arts or youth education. VIA names no medium in its guidelines, and its own grantee roster answers the question directly: photographer Wendy Red Star and film-and-photography artist Amie Siegel both hold 2025 Artistic Production grants. There is no application fee, and the letter of inquiry is filed through VIA's own eligibility form. — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $25,000–$100,000.

item.title: Artist Grant 2026 · The Supporting Act Foundation
item.description: Ten unrestricted grants of €10,000 from the Dutch foundation The Supporting Act, paid in ten monthly instalments of €1,000 from January to October 2027 and intended to cover living costs and artistic development. The grant goes to emerging artists from underrepresented groups whose practice involves collaborative, collective or community-benefiting creative processes; the application form's own discipline picker names photography outright, alongside architecture, dance, design, digital arts, film and video, literature, music, multidisciplinary practice, painting, performing and sculpture, and the independent selection committee is drawn from artists, curators and former grantees. To apply you must have two to ten years of professional experience, have been born in or before 2005, be based in Belgium, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain or the United Kingdom with a bank account in your own name in one of those countries, identify as belonging to an underrepresented group or as someone facing systemic barriers in your country's creative industries, and have a website or public social profile where your work is visible. The application is a form plus links to three publicly available works and a video of no more than four minutes; only finished work is accepted, not project proposals, and one application per person. The call opens 1 September 2026 and closes 1 October at 11:00 CET, all applicants hear back in late October 2026, and the announcement and first instalment follow in January 2027. There is no application fee, no budget required and no spending report afterwards. Current and former TSAF grantees are not eligible. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €10,000.

item.title: 2026 Small Works Exhibition · Charles H. Taylor Visual Arts Center
item.description: Small-works show at Hampton Arts' Charles H. Taylor Visual Arts Center, open to all Hampton regional and Virginia artists aged 18 and over. The call is open to all media; two-dimensional work must be no larger than 8 x 10 inches including the frame and three-dimensional work no larger than 8 inches on any side, with 2D pieces under 20 square inches and 3D pieces under 5 inches cubed judged separately as Miniatures. Work must be original, made within the past two years and not previously shown at the center, and accepted pieces must arrive dry and ready to hang (no sawtooth hangers). One entry per artist covers up to six artworks for $40, or $35 for current Hampton Arts League members. Awards go to First ($200), Second ($150) and Third ($100) Place plus three Awards of Merit across the two categories, and a new $100 Mighty Miniature award for the strongest miniature as chosen by the judge. Notification is by email the week after the deadline; accepted work is delivered to the center November 10-14 and the exhibition runs December 5, 2026 to January 16, 2027, with an artist reception and awards on Saturday, December 5 from 3 to 5 pm. Because the show runs through the holidays, work that sells may be removed at the time of purchase. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $40 (members $35). Prize: $200 First Prize + Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Bodies & Faces: Art of Figure and Portrait · Art League of New Britain
item.description: Juried exhibition of figure and portrait work at the Art League of New Britain, on view October 9 to November 1, 2026 with an opening reception on Friday, October 9 from 6 to 8 pm. The league accepts all original media - it runs its own annual photography juried exhibition - and the binding eligibility clause is about how the work was made rather than the medium: "Works must have been started from life or have included a live model in the process", so a portrait or figure photograph shot from a live subject qualifies. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original, completed in the past three years and not previously exhibited at ALNB, with combined framed width per artwork up to 72 inches. Jurying is hybrid - juror Susan Strauss, a portrait artist of more than thirty years and a professor at Tunxis Community College, selects from unsigned images online for anonymous review, then picks the prize winners in person after drop-off. Four cash awards total $375: $200 first, $100 second, $50 third and a $25 honourable mention. Up to five entries at $25 for the first and $15 for each additional ($15/$10 for ALNB members). Accepted work stays up for the whole run, including anything that sells, and pick-up is November 1-3; labels must be attached and an artist contract signed at drop-off, so the show is in practice for artists who can deliver to New Britain. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: $25 first entry, $15 additional (members $15/$10). Prize: $375 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Musa International Award for Female Photographers 2026
item.description: Eighth edition of the Musa Award, run by the Lecco photography school Musa Fotografia and going international for the first time in 2026. It is a portfolio prize: each entrant may submit up to three projects of 8 to 25 images, in colour or black and white, mixed technique or other media, assembled as a PDF with a project statement and biography. The theme is "Reclaiming the Frame" - repossessing the power to decide what is worth framing and narrating - and the organisers are explicit that the subjects need not be women, since the point is to see the whole world through women's eyes; every genre is welcome, from architecture and reportage to abstraction and nature. Open to female photographers over 18, amateur or professional, resident in a published list of European countries that includes the EU member states plus the UK, Ukraine, Switzerland, Norway, the Balkans and the microstates. The winner's package is substantial: twenty fine-art exhibition prints produced and donated by Fotofabbrica, an exhibition at the Colorno Photo Life Festival, a screening at the Biennale di Fotografia Femminile in Mantova, a half-hour portfolio review with its artistic director Alessia Locatelli, an editorial meeting with Grazia Dell'Oro of the publisher EMUSE, a filmed interview with curator Loredana De Pace, and €200 towards expenses; reportage projects also exhibit at the Festival Off della Fotografia Etica, and Italian entrants compete for a further show at the Festival della Fotografia Italiana. Entry is €25 for one project, €45 for two and €65 for three, paid at registration with the PDF emailed at the same time. Winners are announced in December 2026. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: €25 (1 project) / €45 (2) / €65 (3). Prize: Exhibition + €200 expenses + Portfolio review.

item.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 74 - Editorial Submissions
item.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 74 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. Submissions close 11:59pm EST on 21 November 2026 and the issue is released at 10pm EST on 21 December 2026. Editorials must be unpublished and exclusive to Solstice - work found published elsewhere is pulled and the contributor blacklisted, and accepted work must stay offline until the issue is out. Fashion submissions need a minimum of five outfit changes (beauty submissions, five hair and make-up looks) with at least three finished, retouched photographs of each outfit, and every garment must carry a real brand credit; stylist's own and model's own credits are rejected, including for vintage and second-hand pieces. Website editorials are open year-round and usually publish within two or three working days. There is no submission fee and no payment for editorials; the magazine does not send complimentary print copies but will supply digital tear sheets on request. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants - Cycle 38 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: One-time grants of up to $5,000 for recent unexpected medical, dental and mental-health emergencies, funded by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and administered by NYFA. The eligible Visual Arts category names Photography outright, alongside craft/sculpture, painting and printmaking, and the programme also covers digital/electronic arts, video/film and choreography. Applicants must be 21 or older, reside in the United States, the District of Columbia, a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory, show sustained public-facing artistic activity over the past five years, and meet the income cap - adjusted gross income no greater than $80,000 individual or $160,000 joint, averaged over the last two federal tax returns. Applicants cannot be enrolled in a degree-seeking programme, and cannot have received a Rauschenberg Medical or Dancer Emergency Grant in the past five years. Cycle 38 covers emergencies that began on or after February 1, 2026; applications opened August 18 and close at 5:00 PM ET on September 15, with notification on November 9, 2026. Artists whose medical costs are covered by Medicare or Medicaid may instead request up to $5,000 in documented living expenses. Roughly $148,000 is distributed each cycle and demand outstrips it, so applying is not a guarantee of an award. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000.

item.title: South Carolina State Parks Artist-in-Residence 2027
item.description: A one-week residency in a South Carolina state park, with the park service providing a cabin, a Carolina camper cabin or a campsite; artists may also stay in their own camper or RV at the assigned park. Applications for the 2027 season are accepted September 1-30, 2026, and the programme is open to South Carolina residents and non-residents alike, with collaborative proposals considered. Photography is well represented among past residents: the 2025 cohort included landscape, infrared and night-sky photographer Paul Atkinson at Givhans Ferry and photographer Michael Gambrell at Cheraw. In return each artist donates one original work representative of the stay within 90 days, to be displayed in park cabins and other facilities. Art forms that manipulate or disturb the park's resources, or that use materials from endangered or threatened species, are excluded, and collecting materials from park property is not permitted. Transportation to and from the assigned park is the artist's responsibility, and residents arrange their own reservation once placed; placement depends on the medium each park wants to display. Applications go through ZAPPlication with four images and a $25 fee, and a panel of state park representatives scores entries, keeping a waiting list for cancellations. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: 1-week residency.

item.title: Lakewood Annual Winter Salon 2026 · Lakewood Cultural Center
item.description: The Lakewood Cultural Center's annual salon, a large-scale group exhibition and art market of small, accessibly priced work, running November 6, 2026 to January 2, 2027 with a reception on November 7 from 6 to 8 pm. Photographs are named among the eligible media alongside original painting, drawing, prints and mixed media; reproductions are not accepted. Work must be two-dimensional and no larger than three feet in any direction including the frame, framed and ready to hang with securely attached wire or a cleat system - nothing suspended from the ceiling or standing on the floor. Everything must be for sale and priced at $500 or less, prices cannot be adjusted after entry, and the City of Lakewood takes a 15% commission; artists sign a loan agreement so work is insured while in the Cultural Center's care, and sold work is collected after December 18. Entry is $30 for up to three works. There is no shipping in either direction - work must be hand-delivered to the Lakewood Cultural Center - so in practice the show is limited to artists who can travel to the Denver area. Laine Godsey, the City of Lakewood's Arts Programming Curator, juries the selection. The organiser's own call description sets the schedule as entries accepted on CaFE until Thursday, October 22, 2026 or until the call is full, notification of acceptance by the end of Friday, October 23, and delivery of accepted work during the week of October 26; note that the CaFE record's structured deadline field and one requirement bullet instead give November 6, which is the exhibition's opening day. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: MCAD–Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Early Career Artists 2026/27
item.description: Four unrestricted $10,000 fellowships for early-career visual artists living in Minnesota, administered by the Minneapolis College of Art and Design and funded by the Jerome Foundation, which has run this programme since 1981 and has backed more than two hundred artists through it. Photography is named outright in the eligible media, alongside painting, sculpture, drawing, printmaking, sequential and comic art, public and social practice, conceptual, installation, graffiti, textile, ceramics, glass, bead, metal, paper, and digital video or film presented in an exhibition or installation context; the programme is aimed at artists who can present work in a gallery. Each fellow receives the $10,000 in unrestricted funds plus $1,000 in reimbursement-based professional development money, three studio visits from professional critics (a local curator, a catalogue writer and a national curator), an exhibition at the MCAD Gallery in January to March 2028, a catalogue with a critical essay on their work, a place on a public panel, access to MCAD's facilities and library, and half-price Continuing Education tuition. The fellowship period runs 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2028. Eligibility is tight and worth reading before applying: you must be a legal Minnesota resident for at least a year before the deadline and stay in the state for the whole fellowship, and you must have between two and ten years of generative practice outside any degree programme. Artists with significant recognition may be too established even inside that window. Applications go through Submittable and ask for proof of residency, ten work samples in any mix of image, audio, video and PDF, a resume, an artist statement and a fellowship goals statement — the guidelines ask that you not use AI or ChatGPT to write either statement. An independent three-person jury scores every application, shortlists twenty-five to thirty, then ten finalists who get twenty-minute online studio visits on 12 and 13 November. Staff take no part in the selection, and MCAD-affiliated applicants can never be more than half of any cohort. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Artist in Residence 2027 · Glen Arbor Arts Center
item.description: A two-week residency on the edge of the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore in northern Michigan, offered several times a year by the Glen Arbor Arts Center to give visiting artists a respite from daily responsibilities and concentrated time to work. Photography is named explicitly among the disciplines considered, along with creative writing, visual art, sculpture, fibre arts, ceramics and music. There is no residency fee — housing and studio space are provided free — and the only cost is a non-refundable $35 application fee. Residents stay in a furnished second-floor walk-up apartment with a bedroom, living room, small bath and galley kitchen a short walk from a grocery and restaurants, and bring their own linens and towels; the apartment is not wheelchair accessible, is smoke-free, allows no pets, and art materials may not be used in it. The studio is a restored tool shed at historic Thoreson Farm inside the national lakeshore, 3.7 miles from the arts centre, a rustic seasonal building with a cement floor, overhead lighting, space heaters and some shared equipment. Each residency is a one-person opportunity — groups and collaborative teams are not considered — and residents commit to the full fourteen days, give a community presentation on the second Thursday of their stay, and may be asked, but not required, to donate one work made during the residency to the centre's permanent collection. A car is effectively necessary: Glen Arbor is walkable but the studio is out at the farm and Traverse City is 26 miles away. This round covers the 2027 season, May to October, though July and early August are generally unavailable because the apartment is in use. Visual artists submit six to eight images plus a resume; applications are reviewed straight after the deadline with notification by mid-March. Anyone selected for a Glen Arbor residency in the past three years is not eligible. — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: 2-week residency.

item.title: Photodarium 2028 · Slanted Publishers
item.description: PHOTODARIUM is a tear-off calendar that reveals a new instant photo every day, each with its own little story: the front of each calendar page carries the photograph, the back a short account of how it came about together with the photographer's name, location and URL. Slanted Publishers in Karlsruhe edits the series with Raban Ruddigkeit, and Seltmann Publishers issues it; Boris Kahl is art director and project manager. Submissions must be original scans of instant photos made with a Polaroid SX-70, a 600 or a new Impossible/Polaroid camera — the editors say plainly that they do not accept fakes. Entrants pick up to five favourite calendar days and upload one photo for each, and three photos by different photographers end up competing for any one day. The back-of-page text is treated as part of the submission and will be printed, so the editors warn that a dummy description gets the whole entry refused. Files should be JPG, RGB, 350 dpi at the original size of 88 x 107 mm including the frame. Entry is free; contributors grant Slanted and Seltmann a non-exclusive right to use the photos for the calendars and their promotion, receive a free copy of the calendar if published and a 50 percent discount on further copies, and no financial compensation is paid. The call for entries opens on 1 September 2026 and closes on 25 September 2026, with production and distribution in 2027. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The Print Continuum · East End Arts Council
item.description: East End Arts Council in Riverhead, New York invites printmakers from across the United States to submit to The Print Continuum, a national juried exhibition celebrating the intersection of printmaking's historical traditions and its expanding contemporary practices. A continuum is a spectrum, the council writes, where distinct points are linked by gradual change rather than clear divisions; printmaking is not divided between old and new but is a medium in which history, innovation and experimentation stay in dialogue. Eligible work includes screen printing, relief printing, woodcut, linocut, intaglio, etching, lithography, monotype, collagraph, gel printing, and mixed-media works incorporating hybrid processes on paper, fabric, sculpture or other substrates. Read the medium clause carefully before applying: photography and 3D printing alone are not eligible, but works incorporating those processes within original printmaking or mixed-media pieces will be considered — so photogravure, photopolymer, screenprints made from photographs and photo-based collage are in scope while a straight photographic print is not. Selections are made by artists Ellen Wiener and Bill Albertini, with the exhibition curated by Mich Miller, Head of Printmaking at East End Arts Council. Applications go through CaFE and ask for an artist statement of up to 500 words on creative intent, process and how printmaking contributes to your vision, three to five images with optional detail or installation views, a website or social media link, and an image list. The cap is three submissions of work, each original and not previously shown at East End Arts Council; the three to five images may include multiple views, details or installation shots of those same pieces. There is no size limitation. Selected work hangs at the council's 11 West Gallery from 24 October to 13 December 2026, with an opening reception on 24 October. Awards are $1,000 for first prize, $500 for second and $250 for third. Council members get early access and a 10 percent discount code on the application fee. Read the terms before entering: accepted work must stay available for the whole run and is sold exclusively through the council, which keeps a 50 percent commission from non-members and 30 percent from members, and selected artists arrange and pay for delivery and return themselves. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $30 (10% off for members). Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Hayama Artist Residency 2027
item.description: Hayama Artist Residency sends artists to Hayama, a coastal town of 33,000 on Japan's Miura Peninsula facing Sagami Bay, for four weeks from 1 to 30 June 2027. Founded and directed by curator Dexter Wimberly, the residency is fully funded: a roundtrip flight to Narita or Haneda, a private bedroom in shared accommodation at hôtel ami hayama for the month, and $800 USD toward meals and local transport. Artists are not required to make new work — the programme is built around rest, research and reflection, immersion in Japanese culture, and meeting artists, curators and gallery owners in Japan. A key component is a group exhibition during the stay, hosted with KOKI ARTS, a contemporary gallery in Tokyo's Bakurocho art district, whose director works with the residency's curatorial team on selection, consignment, shipping and insurance. Open to any visual artist over 21 working in any medium, based anywhere in the world; photography sits squarely in scope — past residents include Joiri Minaya, whom the residency describes as working in photography, digital media, film, performance, sculpture, textiles and painting, and Asim Waqif, who has worked in sculpture, site-specific public installation, video and photography. Applications are reviewed by the director and a selection committee, which for 2026 comprised Alexander Berggruen, Francesca Bertolotti-Bailey, Hilary Burt of SOCO Gallery, Kimberli Gant of the Brooklyn Museum and the artist Yoshua Okón. Submit up to 10 samples in any combination of JPEG, audio or video, with links accepted on a one-page PDF. The $95 application fee is waived for first-time applicants who apply again the following year. Applicants are notified by 15 December 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $95 (waived for second-time applicants). Prize: Funded residency + $800 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Winter Residency 2026–27 · Contact Darkroom
item.description: CONTACT Darkroom is a not-for-profit art centre and photographic darkroom in Totnes, Devon, housed in a repurposed abattoir and specialising in black-and-white and colour hand printing. Its winter residency is resource-based: the organisation's own page describes 24-hour-a-day access to fully equipped colour and black-and-white darkrooms, a dedicated workshop room, workspace and an open gallery, for stays of one week to one month between 1 November 2026 and 31 March 2027, with an ideal Friday start. Facilities include a 20-inch RA4 colour processor, three 5x4 black-and-white enlargers, two 5x4 colour enlargers, a large sink, black-and-white film development and an outside suntrap. The residency is designed for emerging and established photographers working on new or existing projects, testing out processes, or making work that responds to the surrounding landscape — the River Dart running from the Dartmoor moorlands to the Atlantic coast. At the end of a residency artists are invited, but not expected, to share work in a small exhibition, talk or workshop; darkroom inductions, guided walks, excursions and local gallery visits can be arranged on request. Applications are open internationally to artists working across photography, film and lens-based practices, and to those making interdisciplinary work engaging image-making, print and alternative processes. There is no application fee, and no closing date is published: complete the form on the residency page with your preferred dates and an outline of your intentions, and the darkroom will arrange a video call. Applications are considered on a rolling basis for stays inside that November–March window. The residency itself is self-funded at £500 per week for one week, £450 per week for two and £400 per week for three weeks or more; inductions to colour and black-and-white printing are charged separately, and private lodging within walking distance is around £50 per night. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free to apply (£400–£500 per week, self-funded). Prize: Darkroom residency.

item.title: art·i·face · midwest nice art
item.description: art·i·face is a juried open call from midwest nice art, the Sioux Falls artist-run curatorial platform, open to artists internationally who work with materials in a surprising manner. Most utilitarian objects have a specific use; the brief asks how artists transform that purpose, citing Robert Rauschenberg's combines, El Anatsui's bottle-cap wall hangings, Ingrid Calame's paintings traced from forgotten stains on the street, and Rachel Whiteread's unconventional casting sculptures. Artists are asked to consider a secondary use or process within their work — jigs, templates, casts, moulds, scraps, detritus and found objects — used as a way of working, as subject matter, or as a route to abstraction. midwest nice art runs all-media themed shows, and the entry form asks only for the title, medium, size and year of each work; photography runs throughout the gallery's exhibition archive, whose credit lines include archival pigment prints, photographic collage and photographs on paper. The juror is Andrew Nordin, an artist and educator who teaches studio art and art history at Ridgewater College and curates its galleries; he holds BFAs in Painting and Graphic Design from St. Cloud State University and an MFA in Pictorial Arts from San José State University, received a 2017 Minnesota State Arts Board award, and recently completed a residency at Natthagen Art Center in Julussdalen, Norway. Up to three works may be submitted for a $5 exhibition fee, paid via Square once the entry form is completed. Images should be 300 dpi and 1500 px on the longest side. The online exhibition opens 15 December 2026. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Interpretation of Dreams · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on dream states and interior worlds. Photography is often seen as a record of what is real, but Praxis frames it as a portal into the imagined, the unconscious and the symbolic — where time folds, logic dissolves, and meaning slips through what is revealed and what is withheld. Submissions may encompass constructed realities, surreal compositions, symbolic gestures, lyrical narratives and emotionally resonant abstractions; the gallery welcomes images that feel like fragments of the subconscious, poetic, uncanny or mythic, and states that all lens-based artwork is welcome. Curated by the Praxis directors rather than a guest juror. Up to 38 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (17 October – 14 November 2026) and featured on the gallery's online exhibition page. Awards are a Directors' Choice (free entry into two future juried calls of the artist's choice) and five honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery. Images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames, and retains a 50% commission on any sales. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Annual Juried Members Show · Art Center Sarasota
item.description: The Annual Juried Members Show at Art Center Sarasota — a 501(c)(3) art centre on Sarasota Bay with four galleries, in its 2025–26 centennial season — is free from a prescribed theme and welcomes original work in all media, with the call naming painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, mixed media, digital arts, sculpture and video. Every current member who submits is guaranteed inclusion, so the jurying decides the awards rather than the hang: Swiss-born Sarasota muralist Alissa Silvers reviews all required information except the artist's name and the artwork price, and selects the awards in person once the show is installed. Awards are 1st place $500, 2nd $300, 3rd $200, plus two Merit Awards and four Honorable Mentions. Work must be original, completed within the last three years and not previously shown at the centre; editioned prints are eligible where labelled and numbered, which the call spells out as covering photography, and copies or reproductions are not. 2D work is capped at 30 × 30 inches after framing. All work must be for sale, with the artist keeping 60% of the selling price. Membership runs from $25 a year for students and $75 for individuals. The exhibition runs 3 December 2026 – 9 January 2027 with an opening reception on the 3rd; accepted work is received in person on 17–18 November or must arrive by post between 16 and 18 November. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $30 (1 work), $40 (2), $45 (3); students $10/$20/$25. Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: TRANSLUCENT · Manifest Gallery
item.description: An international call from Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati for works that employ, depict, or explore translucency and transparency. The gallery names glass, acrylic, plastic, stacks of layers, gossamer weaves, lenses and filters among the materials, subjects and mechanisms that may pierce, reveal and distort, and frames the show as an exhibit of ideas, images, materials and mechanisms that ask you to see through. Open to everyone internationally and to all traditional and non-traditional genre and media, with no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery door and no restriction on when the work was made. Selection is two-stage: an anonymous multi-member panel of professional and academic advisors juries the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibition curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, and one work from each of the nine exhibition periods in Manifest's 23rd season wins a $1,000 Grand Jury Award decided by a second-round re-jury of the top-scoring works. Selected work is shown December 11, 2026 to January 8, 2027 and documented in the season annual; artists receive 70% on sales. Entry is $45 for up to three works and $5 for each additional work, with no cap on the number of entries, and the prospectus states this jury fee is the only cost charged by Manifest for participation. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: TAPPED 2026 — 17th Annual · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest Gallery's long-running annual exhibit of works by artists shown side by side with works by their current or former instructors, celebrating the legacy of the academic process in art. Now in its 17th year, TAPPED is not a call for collaborative work: each member of a pair submits their own entry form, fee and images, and names the other on their form, with at least as many works submitted as there are companions named. Media is open to all traditional and non-traditional genre and media, including but not limited to sculpture, photography, painting, drawing and printmaking, and the works by each person need not relate in theme, media or style to the other's. The gallery notes that three-way connections — someone tapping both a former teacher and a current or former student — are especially welcome. An anonymous multi-member panel of professional and academic advisors juries the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibition curator, who makes the final selections. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, one work from each of the nine exhibition periods in Manifest's 23rd season wins a $1,000 Grand Jury Award, and artists receive 70% on sales. Selected work is shown December 11, 2026 to January 8, 2027. Entry is $45 for up to three works plus $5 for each additional work, with no cap on the number of entries. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: The Manifest Prize 2026 — 17th Annual · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest Gallery's annual competitive award, in which a several-round blind jury reduces an international field to a single work: the winner receives $10,000 in cash and a four-week solo exhibit of that one work, hung in a gallery of its own alongside juror and artist statements. As many as 18 purposely anonymous professional jurors score the entries. Four runner-up works each receive $250 and are published in the Manifest Exhibition Annual. The prize was doubled from $5,000 to $10,000 in 2025 and is entirely separate from the season's nine $1,000 Grand Jury Awards. Media is open to any and all traditional and non-traditional visual arts genre and media, explicitly including photography, video, sculpture, installation, painting, drawing and printmaking, with no size limit and no stylistic preference — the gallery notes that very small works and room-sized works have both won in past years. The only substantive limits are that work must have been completed within the past five years (2021–2026) and must be available for the exhibition period. The winning work is unveiled on December 10, 2026 at a ticketed preview event and shown December 11, 2026 to January 8, 2027; work need not be for sale, and artists receive 70% if it is. Entry is $45 for up to five works by September 15 and $60 for up to five works from September 16 to the final October 6 deadline, plus $5 for each additional work. — Deadline: October 6, 2026. Fee: $60 (5 images) + $5 each; $45 early to Sep 15. Prize: $10,000 + solo exhibition.

item.title: Focus #7 — The Pursuit of Happiness · Les Mesnographies
item.description: Annual open call for Les Mesnographies, the first free open-air photography festival in the Yvelines, staged in the municipal park at Les Mesnuls west of Paris. For its 7th edition the festival invites series responding to the notion of happiness, quoting Oxford's Department of Psychology — happiness as a positive emotion arising not only from doing or receiving something but from a sense of connection between people or of wellbeing — and asking what happiness is: a goal, a state to be reached, something within us or something built over time. The festival hangs work outdoors in the park for three weeks each year, brings together photographers of different nationalities, and runs alongside a free programme of guided visits, talks, a picnic and an opening concert; past editions have shown photographers from Argentina, China and France, and the festival has been covered by M Le Monde, Fisheye, Télérama, Polka, Beaux Arts, France Culture and Arte. It also runs a hors-les-murs strand placing work in nearby communes with the Parc naturel régional de la Haute Vallée de Chevreuse. Applications are a single PDF of no more than 20 images with the series text and a biography, sent by email — the organisers ask that you do not send WeTransfer links. Because the work is shown outdoors in a park open to all audiences including children, the festival asks applicants to keep that in mind when building a series. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Open-air festival exhibition.

item.title: CANINE · Maine Museum of Photographic Arts
item.description: The Maine Museum of Photographic Arts is gathering work for CANINE, an upcoming exhibition it announces with a single word and a William Wegman print. Submissions go by email rather than through a portal: send six to twelve JPEGs sized to 1500 pixels on the longest edge, a short bio of two or three sentences, an artist statement of three to five sentences about the content of the work, and an image list, with 'CANINE SUBMISSION' in the subject line. The museum asks for conceptual fine art images only. No fee is attached to the call. The exhibition is underwritten by the family of Jamie Salomon (1963-2024), a photographer who took up his father's Rolleiflex at twelve, earned a BFA in photography from the School of Visual Arts in New York and built a career in Maine across architectural, editorial and commercial work; an avid nature enthusiast, his knowledge of the woods, oceans and wildlife ran through his pictures. Established in 2010, MMPA is the only museum in Maine dedicated exclusively to photography, artist-run and directed by Denise Froehlich, exhibiting and collecting photographic work and selling contemporary and secondary-market prints through its gallery. It has moved into a new home at 387 Commercial Street in Portland, open Tuesday to Saturday from 11am to 5pm. Submissions close on Tuesday, December 1, 2026. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Pile Press Literary + Art Journal, Issue 13
item.description: Pile Press is an alternative publishing collective in Portland, Oregon making local and limited-edition print publications, and its bi-annual literary and arts journal is open for Issue 13. The journal carries poetry, art, short fiction, creative nonfiction, photography and comics by women and non-binary creatives, and submissions are open only to US residents identifying as women and/or non-binary. Photographers and artists may send up to three pieces, at 300 DPI or better. Simultaneous submissions are allowed as long as you tell the editors promptly if the work is taken elsewhere; previously published work is not accepted, though the press does not count social media as formal publication. There is no payment on publication, but contributors get a contributor rate on the journal and the reach of a title stocked in several bookshops around Portland. Entry costs $4 through Submittable and the reading period runs from August 15 to September 25, 2026. The press also runs CHUNK, a black-and-white Oregon-centric broadside paper open to Oregon residents of any gender on a rolling basis. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $4. Prize: Publication.
